title: Edison Volunteer Builds a Passion for Giving Back
summary: A member of SCE’s Corporate Security team helps build 17 homes for families in the San Gabriel Valley.
body_markdown:
Addison Coniglio, a member of Southern California Edison’s Corporate Security team, is often referred to as the ultimate volunteer.


Since his first event with[Habitat for Humanity](https://secure.habitat.org/site/Donation2?mfc_pref=T&df_id=8956&8956.donation=form1&s_src=DNAJ26114169901&s_subsrc=General&utm_medium=cpc&utm_source=bing&utm_campaign=tg&utm_content=brandnone&mrkgadid=&mrkgcl=1005&mrkgen=&mrkgbflag=&mrkgcat=&acctid=21700000001719422&device=c&network=o&matchtype=e&locationid=%7bloc_phyiscal_ms%7d&creative=&targetid=kwd-79165477384298:loc-190&campaignid=506254237&adgroupid=1266639193204054&gclid=4b4880b45004180ce3eaea4bf52f975d&gclsrc=3p.ds&&gclid=4b4880b45004180ce3eaea4bf52f975d&gclsrc=3p.ds&msclkid=4b4880b45004180ce3eaea4bf52f975d) in 2020, Coniglio has clocked more than 800 hours helping build 17 homes for families in need.


"I started out because I was interested in construction," said Coniglio. "But then I met the families, built relationships and saw the impact these homes have on their lives. That's what keeps me coming back.”


As a volunteer crew lead for San Gabriel Valley Habitat for Humanity, Addison Coniglio (back center) guides volunteers during construction at a build site in the San Gabriel Valley.


Coniglio first learned about the organization from a friend who invited him to join a build with the San Marcos chapter while he was living in San Diego, but it wasn't until he moved to the San Gabriel Valley that he began volunteering on a regular basis. Now, he rarely misses a weekend.


His first event locally was in Pasadena cleaning up a property that was once a closed-down liquor store. Known in the community as "Blood Corner," it had long been associated with gang activity and repeated fires.


Offering a fresh start, Habitat transformed the corner into a home ownership opportunity for two families, including a veteran and a social worker.


"When we showed up, there was nothing but a blank slab," he said. "By the end of the day, we had built 26 feet of walls from scratch. It was incredibly satisfying. I got to learn something, help people and be part of a good cause. I was hooked.”


As Coniglio’s involvement with[San Gabriel Valley Habitat for Humanity](https://sgvhabitat.org/) began to grow, his role did too.


Within his first six months, he became a crew lead, helping train and mentor new volunteers on build sites. Soon after, he was asked to be an SGV Habitat ambassador, supporting outreach efforts and connecting community members with opportunities to get involved.


A rendering of the Addison, a Habitat for Humanity home model named after Southern California Edison employee and longtime volunteer Addison Coniglio.


The skills he picked up along the way have paid off at home, too. He used his Habitat experience to remodel his own home single-handedly.


He has poured so much of himself into the organization that Habitat even named one of its home models after him — dubbed the Addison.


"What makes Addison special isn't just the number of hours he's volunteered," said Bryan Wong, CEO of San Gabriel Valley Habitat for Humanity. "It's the way he connects with people, celebrates with families, stays in touch long after the homes are finished, and shows up again and again because he believes everyone deserves a safe place to call home."


Over the last six years, Coniglio has had a hand in helping change the lives of 17 families in his community, and he has no plans to slow down anytime soon. While the construction originally piqued his interest, now his favorite part is what comes after the build.


“I cry like a baby at every dedication ceremony," Addison said. "Watching the families get their keys — it’s difficult not to get emotional."
